OECD Future of Education and Skills 2030
Position Paper on Artificial Intelligence Literacy in Schools

This report examines how compulsory education systems are preparing
learners aged 6 to 18 for a world shaped by artificial intelligence. It
draws on country surveys, expert interviews and a review of national
curricula across member states.

Key findings

Schools that embed AI literacy across the curriculum report stronger
critical thinking among primary school students than schools that teach
it as a stand-alone unit.

Sustained collaboration between teachers and learners improves the
uptake of digital competence in lower-secondary classrooms.

The report notes that many systems still lack a coherent framework for
assessing creativity as a future skill.

Methodology

Data were collected through a survey of education ministries and a
structured review of curriculum documents. The findings are descriptive
and should be read as policy guidance rather than causal evidence.
